A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HRM has a potentially vital, but so far unrealised role to play in the development and implementation of a company's sustainability and social responsibility strategy.

we propose an approach to sustainable HR that is multidimensional (in terms of the HR activities that contribute to CS/CSR) and multi stakeholder in nature (i.e. HRM should take into account the interests of a broader set stakeholders than just the employees and their immediate managers).

the current crisis of legitimacy and the need to tackle grand challenges require HRM to take a much more active and prominent role in corporate sustainability and CSR efforts, but that this requires a shift from a narrow focus on the economic dimension of the triple bottom line to a broader perspective that encompasses all stakeholders and the social and environmental dimensions of the triple bottom-line.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HRM can be a key contributor to CS/CSR, but only if the field adopts a broader, more multidimensional and multi stakeholder perspective on HRM.

HRM can play an instrumental role in the design, implementation, and monitoring of a firm's CSR/CS activities, but only if it is able to overcome a series of barriers that currently hinder its effectiveness.
HRM can play an important role in the design of CS/CSR strategy, but that the current state of the art in the literature is insufficient to support this role.
